header.heading:
Real numbers up front.

header.lead: Pricing varies a lot by trade. Handyman work is hourly, small electrical is flat-rate, and remodels are project-quoted after a free in-home estimate. Below: the actual ballpark numbers per category, how estimates work, and what you should expect to see on a written quote.

billing.monthlyNote: your specific cost depends on the job and materials

groups.label: Handyman, Electrical, Remodel & Exterior
groups.blurb: Three ways to think about pricing across our four trades. Hourly for handyman, flat-rate for small electrical, project-quoted for remodel and bigger exterior work. Written quote before any work starts in every category.

tiers.name: Handyman (Hourly)
tiers.description: General home repairs, drywall, doors, fixture installs, mounting, and punch-list work. $95/hr with a one-hour minimum, or $85/hr in 4-hour blocks for bigger punch-list days. Materials at cost plus a small handling markup, listed on your written quote before work starts.

features.name: Phone-quotes from photos for clear-cut jobs
Materials at cost plus small handling markup
Branded truck, written quote, photos at end-of-job

tiers.name: Electrical (Flat + Quoted)
tiers.description: Small electrical is flat-rate so you know the price before we start. Standard outlet add on existing circuit $185, standard ceiling fan install on existing fixture box $295. Bigger work — panel upgrades, EV chargers, generator transfer switches — quoted on-site after a free walkthrough.

features.name: Ceiling fan install (existing fixture box) — $295 flat
Licensed KS electrical contractor on every job (#E-19842)
Permits pulled and inspections coordinated where required

tiers.name: Light Remodel (Project)
tiers.description: Kitchens, baths, and basement finish-outs in the $5k–$60k range. Free in-home estimate, written scope and price within 3–5 business days, on-site supervisor every workday. We're not the right call for whole-house gut renovations or new builds — we're a small crew that does mid-size projects well.

oneOff.heading: How an estimate is prepared.
oneOff.body: After your in-home estimate walkthrough, we put a written scope and price together within 3–5 business days. The quote covers labor, materials at cost, any permits and inspections, and a line-by-line breakdown of what's included and what's not. You sign nothing at the walkthrough — the quote goes home with you and you accept on your timeline. More on the FAQ →

faqs.question: Why don't you list every project price on the website?
faqs.answer: Because the same kitchen remodel can be $12k or $50k depending on cabinets, counters, layout changes, and what's behind the walls. Posting a single number would be misleading. We give real ranges per category here, and a written project price after we've walked the space.

faqs.question: Is the in-home estimate really free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Free in-home estimates on remodel projects and bigger electrical work. The only thing we charge for is dispatch on jobs where the customer cancels after the truck is already on-site, and we always disclose that up front. Phone-quotes are free for handyman and small electrical work.

faqs.question: Do you offer payment plans on remodels?
faqs.answer: We use milestone payments on remodel projects — a deposit at signing, payments through the project tied to specific milestones, and a final payment at walkthrough. We don't do third-party financing, but milestone structures make most projects manageable without it.

faqs.question: What's included on a written quote?
faqs.answer: Line items for labor, materials at cost (with brand info on key items), any permits and inspections, exclusions called out explicitly, and a section for known-unknowns we'd hit a change-order on. The price is the price unless we hit something hidden in the walls — and if we do, we tell you immediately and you sign before the cost changes.

cta.heading: Have questions about pricing or scope?
cta.body: The walkthrough is the right place to talk numbers on a remodel project. The phone or text is the right place to phone-quote handyman or small electrical work. Either way, written quote before any work starts.
